title: Sort by weight
summary: Compare the reading of a scale with a limit and send heavy boxes to the side belt and light boxes straight on.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show scale accuracy.
objectives: Classify an item by comparing an analog value with a limit.
Read the value only when the scale says it is stable.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/WeightSorter.st, run the belts after Start and hold each box on the scale with the blade. When Stable is TRUE, compare Weight with 3.5 kg: push a heavier box onto the side belt, release a lighter one by lowering the blade for 2.5 s.
stages.checkpoint: Heavy boxes end in HeavyBin, light boxes in LightBin, and Green lights after twelve boxes.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, think about what Weight reads while a box is still moving, and why the program waits for Stable. Which of the two box masses, 2 kg and 5 kg, lies on which side of 3.5 kg?
stages.checkpoint: Weight is 0 until the box rests; the decision is taken once, on the first scan with Stable TRUE, and the infeed stops while the pusher works.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}: The starter drives no output, so no belt moves and no box is weighed; run the belts after Start, hold each box on the scale and send it to the bin its weight selects.
stages.checkpoint: Check reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press Run (F5) and open the 3D view.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named weight-sorting and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the 3D view and the Weight reading: it jumps from 0 to 2 or 5 kg when the box settles. A 5 kg box is pushed out; a 2 kg box rides on after the blade goes down.
stages.checkpoint: The pusher goes out and back once per heavy box, and the infeed belt stands still during the stroke.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The grade cannot compare numbers: it sees which bin each box ended in. Any limit between 2 kg and 5 kg passes, so the 3.5 kg of the task is yours to justify, not the grade.
stages.checkpoint: A box that arrives in the wrong bin fails the ALWAYS assertion.

hints.text: Use a step number: 0 wait for a stable box, 1 push, 2 retract, 3 release. Take Heavy := Weight > 3.5 only when you leave step 0.
The blade stays down in step 3 for 2.5 s (a TON); Hold := Active AND Step <> 3. Count the boxes with a CTU of 12 and drive Green from its Q.

faultCases: The starter drives no output, so no belt moves and no box is weighed; run the belts after Start, hold each box on the scale and send it to the bin its weight selects.
